headline: WNBA Finals Game 4: Valkyries stun Dream 67-62 to level series 2-2
whyCareReason: Golden State staved off elimination with a gritty 67-62 road win, tying the Finals 2-2 and forcing Game 5 in San Francisco.
teaser: FINAL: Valkyries 67, Dream 62. Williams 17 pts, Hayes 13 pts. Series tied 2-2 heading to Chase Center.
story: The Golden State Valkyries refused to let their dream season end on Saturday, 24 October, overcoming a hostile crowd at State Farm Arena to upset the Atlanta Dream 67-62 in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals. The victory leveled the best-of-five series at 2-2 and earned the expansion franchise a winner-take-all Game 5 on their home floor in San Francisco. Gabby Williams spearheaded Golden State with 17 points, five rebounds and three steals, while Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton added 13 points apiece. Golden State's swarming interior defense clamped down on Angel Reese, snapping her streak of three straight Finals double-doubles by holding her to eight points on 2-of-12 shooting. Rhyne Howard paced Atlanta with 19 points, but the Dream went cold down the stretch.
stakes: The Finals head to a decisive Game 5 in San Francisco after Golden State fought off elimination in Atlanta.
rivalryAngle: Expansion Valkyries battle back from the brink to set up a winner-take-all showdown at Chase Center.
funFacts: Game 4 Final: Golden State Valkyries 67, Atlanta Dream 62.
Series tied 2-2: Game 1 Valkyries 68-64; Game 2 Dream 79-65; Game 3 Dream 97-71; Game 4 Valkyries 67-62.
Decisive Game 5 moves back to Chase Center in San Francisco.
